paper.title: MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning-to-Action Security of MLLM-Based Mobile Agents under Cross-Modal Consistency Injection
paper.central_claim: MobileInject is the first benchmark for multimodal (visual+textual) indirect injection and reasoning-to-action security of MLLM-based mobile agents: 108 executable, resettable Android-emulator instances (11 scenarios, 9 risk categories) with deterministic state oracles; Cross-Modal Consistency Injection (CMCI) reveals a cross-modal reinforcement effect, two reinforced attacks (MRCD, RCI) intensify trust manipulation and reasoning hijacking, and a Reasoning Security Diagnosis Framework (RSDF) shows agents are broadly vulnerable with many failures stemming from early reasoning hijacking.

provenance.session_note: actual_model taken from the worker system prompt (Sonnet 5.5, claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]); no session id / receipt exposed to the worker, so null

materials.note: HTML text render (73,100 chars) read in full including all tables; figures (Fig 1-12) are not in the text; no appendix in this render, so prompts/templates/oracle code/diagnoser model are not visible.

evidence.quote: we introduce MobileInject, the first benchmark for evaluating mobile agents against multimodal injection attacks and reasoning-to-action security risks.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim ('first' is not verifiable from the text).

evidence.quote: MobileInject provides a high-fidelity interactive mobile evaluation framework covering 11 scenarios, 9 security-risk categories, and 108 executable risk instances.
evidence.support_explanation: Scale of the resource.

evidence.quote: Consequently, attack success alone is insufficient to characterize the end-to-end security of mobile agents from safety awareness to action execution.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: outcome-only evaluation.

evidence.quote: First, many benchmarks rely on unrealistic sandbox environments
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap (realism); judged via Table 1 checklist, not by running neighbours.

evidence.quote: Nevertheless, existing evaluations still lack a systematic benchmark for multimodal indirect injection in realistic mobile ecosystems.
evidence.support_explanation: Positioning vs MobileSafetyBench, GhostEI-Bench, OS-Sentinel, AgentDoG, AgentDojo.

evidence.quote: Attacker can inject malicious payloads only through these observable surfaces, but cannot alter the system prompt, model parameters, operating system, or genuine user instructions.
evidence.support_explanation: Black-box, trusted-instruction/untrusted-observation threat model.

evidence.quote: First, MobileInject constructs a high-fidelity Android environment based on a full-function emulator, covering 11 application scenarios, 108 executable risk instances, and 9 security-risk categories, to characterize realistic multi-step and cross-application execution processes.
evidence.support_explanation: Environment is an Android emulator; fidelity to real devices is asserted, not measured.

evidence.quote: MobileInject executes each instance in a resettable Android emulator rather than as a static prompt–response sample.
evidence.support_explanation: Online, resettable, stateful execution.

evidence.quote: Admission requires schema completeness, successful reset, payload visibility in the declared channel, executable benign and adversarial paths, and replayable oracle checks.
evidence.support_explanation: Instance admission/quality control.

evidence.quote: Because the 108 instances reuse workflow and objective structures, they are not semantically or statistically independent; our analysis accounts for both dependencies.
evidence.support_explanation: 108 instances = reused workflow x objective structure; effective sample is smaller.

evidence.quote: The stress layer defines 12 registered adversarial objectives spanning nine consequence categories
evidence.support_explanation: 12 objectives x 9 workflows = 108.

evidence.quote: CMCI varies where the same adversarial instruction is exposed: the visual channel only, the textual channel only, or both.
evidence.support_explanation: The manipulated axis.

evidence.quote: Fig. 11 then fixes the exposure count: repeating text changes AGR from 68.8% to 72.9%, and repeating the visual payload leaves AGR at 27.8%, whereas presenting the same content once in each channel reaches 85.4% AGR and 0.0% UA.
evidence.support_explanation: Equal-exposure control isolating the cross-modal effect.

evidence.quote: Equal-exposure CMCI controls on Gemini-2.5-Flash, averaged over four major benign workflows.
evidence.support_explanation: The decisive control is one model and four workflows.

evidence.quote: Among the 108 paired instances, 30 exhibit the same reversal pattern: neither VOI nor TOI reaches the adversarial state, whereas aligned CMCI does.
evidence.support_explanation: Matched-trajectory evidence (30/108).

evidence.quote: Their AGR ranges from 70.83% to 77.08%, whereas the full setting reaches 85.40% with 0.00% UA.
evidence.support_explanation: Budget-matched controls (length, repetition, exposure, salience) for MRCD+RCI.

evidence.quote: Fig. 9 shows that adding RCI raises AGR by 5.6–16.7 percentage points across all six base attacks while reducing UA in every comparison.
evidence.support_explanation: RCI ablation.

evidence.quote: an automated semantic evaluator separate from the tested mobile agent proposes the diagnostic vector
evidence.support_explanation: RSDF awareness/rationale/action labels come from an LLM evaluator whose identity is not stated in the text.

evidence.quote: Awareness requires an explicit link to the injected source, conflict, or risk; generic caution is insufficient.
evidence.support_explanation: Labelling rubric for SAR.

evidence.quote: The implemented pipeline additionally enforces that an episode whose adversarial state oracle fires contains at least one action-hijack label and, when rationale is available, at least one rationale-hijack label
evidence.support_explanation: Outcome constraint: RHR/AHR are forced to be consistent with the oracle, which inflates their coupling by construction.

evidence.quote: They are verified against Android/application state rather than inferred from the tested agent’s response.
evidence.support_explanation: Deterministic state oracles for UA and AGR.

evidence.quote: OSS ranges from 0 to 100 and summarizes the outcome and trajectory dimensions with fixed weights
evidence.support_explanation: Auxiliary OSS has ad hoc weights (40/20/20/20).

evidence.quote: every complete framework–model condition has N = 108 N=108 episodes
evidence.support_explanation: N=108 per condition (9 models x 2 frameworks).

evidence.quote: execute up to 20 agent actions while logging each observation, rationale, parsed action, target, and state transition
evidence.support_explanation: Equal step budget of 20 actions for all conditions.

evidence.quote: For supported comparisons, we report cluster-paired inference; for the remaining conditions, we report point estimates over the full grid.
evidence.support_explanation: Statistics: cluster-paired inference only for some comparisons.
UC column (clean utility) takes values 100/88.89/77.78/66.67/44.44 (multiples of 1/9, one 75.00): our inference is that UC rests on about nine benign workflows.

evidence.quote: Average UA is only 17.59% under MobAgent and 11.11% under M3A, while AGR remains high at 51.13% and 50.31%.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline vulnerability numbers.

evidence.quote: Low AGR can reflect weak execution ability rather than genuine reasoning-level resistance.
evidence.support_explanation: Own caveat showing why outcome-only AGR misleads; motivates RSDF.

evidence.quote: For GLM-4.5V, RHR and AHR are identical in both frameworks (98.15%/98.15% and 99.07%/99.07%), showing strong reasoning–action coupling.
evidence.support_explanation: Coupling claim; identical values are partly forced by E020.

evidence.quote: These families map to 9 top-level risk consequences, including the merger of content tampering and data destruction under data-integrity compromise.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 7 shows 10 categories; the paper merges two to get 9 (reporting inconsistency).

evidence.quote: Table 9 shows that the evaluated prompt-level defenses provide only limited protection under MobileInject.
evidence.support_explanation: Defense claim; all five defenses are prompt-level and run on GLM-4.5V/MobAgent (Table 9 baseline).

evidence.quote: SCoT reduces AGR by 12.96 points, yet its cluster interval crosses zero
evidence.support_explanation: Best defense effect is not statistically distinguishable from zero.

evidence.quote: Fig. 5 reports empirical repeated-run variances of at most 2.15 for the displayed RSDF metrics and 3.85 for the displayed endpoint metrics on the 0–100 scale
evidence.support_explanation: Repeatability of some metrics; sample of reruns is small.

evidence.quote: The directory labels for the 2026 and 2028 files are swapped, so we use the embedded seed rather than the folder name.
evidence.support_explanation: Data-handling slip disclosed; three seeds for GLM-4.5V/MobAgent endpoints only.

signatures.object: Poisoned observation pair (visual screenshot content, textual UI/XML representation) of an Android workflow; baseline: single-channel textual (TOI) or visual (VOI) injection
signatures.information: Attacker controls only observable carriers (rendered content and UI metadata); cannot touch system prompt, model, OS or user instruction. Agents see screenshot + UI/XML.
signatures.operation: Embed the same registered adversarial instruction in the visual carrier, the textual carrier, or both (CMCI), with equal-exposure controls (TOI+, VOI+ repeat twice in one channel).
signatures.output: Endpoint pair (benign oracle, adversarial oracle) per episode; AGR, UA, OCM.
signatures.conditions: Payload visible in the declared channel (admission rule); 20-action budget; resettable snapshot.
signatures.selection_rule: not_applicable for retention; instance admission by contract checks
signatures.persistence: Benchmark release (108 instances); not a learning system.
signatures.claimed_effect: Cross-modal reinforcement: CMCI 85.4% AGR vs 72.9% (text x2) and 27.8% (visual x2) on Gemini-2.5-Flash.
signatures.failure_boundary: Single model/four workflows for the control; non-adaptive carriers; dependent instances.

signatures.object: Attack templates under a fixed adversarial objective: MRCD (role-like authority/consent/rationale fragments) and RCI (context-anchored bridge making the goal switch look like the next step)
signatures.information: Visible current-app context; registered adversarial GoalID; no model internals.
signatures.operation: Compose authority/priority/consent cues and a pseudo-rationale bridge into the carrier text.
signatures.output: Higher AGR and lower UA than six base attacks and budget-matched baselines (InjecAgent+, Manipulation+, Important+).
signatures.conditions: Matched length, objective repetitions, exposure rounds and interface salience.
signatures.claimed_effect: +5.6 to +16.7 pp AGR from RCI; full setting 85.40% vs 70.83-77.08% for matched baselines (Gemini-2.5-Flash).
signatures.failure_boundary: Not tested against adaptive/informed defenders; only prompt defenses evaluated.

signatures.object: Trajectory-level diagnosis: RSDF (collector, two deterministic state oracles, LLM Reasoning Diagnoser, aggregator, reporter)
signatures.information: Post-exposure observation, emitted rationale, action, target and resulting device state; evaluator is separate from the tested agent.
signatures.operation: Oracles give (benign, adversarial) endpoints; an LLM evaluator proposes awareness / rationale-hijack / action-hijack labels with trace anchors; a conflict checker and adjudication merge them; outcome constraints force labels to agree with the oracle.
signatures.output: UC, UA, AGR, OCM, SAR, RHR, RHOR, RHD, AHR, AHAS, RATM and the OSS summary.
signatures.conditions: Rationale available in the recorded trace.
signatures.claimed_effect: Shows reasoning hijack precedes harmful action (RHR 75-81% average) and low AGR can hide hijacked reasoning.
signatures.failure_boundary: Evaluator identity and human agreement not reported; outcome constraints couple RHR and AHR with AGR.

gap.author_gap: Existing agent-security evaluations are unrealistic sandboxes, lack multimodal indirect injection in mobile ecosystems, and report only binary success so they cannot show risk awareness, reasoning hijack or action propagation.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete, testable residue: whether synchronized visual+textual exposure amplifies injection beyond repeated single-channel exposure, and whether outcome-only metrics mask hijacked reasoning. Both are probed with controls. The neighbour comparison (GhostEI-Bench, MobileSafetyBench, OS-Sentinel, AgentDoG) rests on the authors' feature checklist (Table 1), not on running those benchmarks. Note dual-channel exposure is the natural condition for on-screen text (it also appears in UI/XML), so 'cross-modal consistency' partly describes ordinary exposure.
lineage: Tool-agent injection benchmarks (InjecAgent, AgentDojo) -> mobile/GUI safety benchmarks (MobileSafetyBench, GhostEI-Bench, OS-Sentinel, AgentDoG, DTAP) -> MobileInject (dual-channel injection, reinforced templates, trajectory diagnosis)

rs_pattern.reason: Operation executed: name the measurement confound (repeated exposure vs cross-modal placement; outcome-only AGR hiding hijacked reasoning), build instances where one axis moves (visual/textual/both with equal-exposure controls, length/repetition/salience-matched baselines), and score with oracles independent of the agent; the headline is the divergence between apparent and de-confounded outcomes. Supporting: MRCD/RCI violate the trusted-instruction/untrusted-observation boundary agents rely on (exploit-type pivot).
rs_pattern.executes_pattern: yes for the controlled-instance part; partial for independent ground truth (state oracles yes; RSDF diagnostic labels no) and for the scope/transfer step (single-model controls, emulator only).
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partially evidenced: matched controls show an effect on one model; whether it holds across models and for natural exposure is not shown, and the reasoning-coupling claim is partly constructed by outcome-constrained labelling.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: C02 steps: (1) name the confound - met (repeated exposure; outcome-only metrics); (2) controlled instances varying one axis - met (TOI/VOI/TOI+/VOI+/CMCI; matched MRCD/RCI baselines; 30/108 matched reversals) but the central control uses one model and four workflows; (3) ground truth independent of the evaluand - partial (deterministic state oracles yes; LLM-diagnosed rationale/action labels are outcome-constrained and not human-validated); (4) divergence as headline - met (low AGR vs high RHR, GLM-4.6V M3A 14.81% AGR vs 77.78% RHR); (5) scope bounded/transfer shown - partial (emulator-only, 108 dependent instances, templated carriers).

unmet: human validation of the LLM diagnoser
failure_modes_present: synthetic/contrived carriers with unshown transfer to natural exposure

matches.reason: The benchmark's value rests on controlled one-axis contrasts reported as divergences; C02 is its sole sibling under the parent.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Audit-and-pivot success conditions: exploit success traced to a structural property (visual grounding + textual executability produce a priority switch) - partial; validated against an adaptive/informed defender - unmet (only static prompt defenses); prior methods shown to fail because of the audited assumption - partial (single-channel evaluation misses the effect). Sub-cards C01/C05/C11/C19/C28/C29 concern representational loci, identifiability, selection rules or optimisation theory, none matching, so sub=null.
matches.reason: Needed to account for MRCD/RCI as boundary-violating attack constructions distinct from the diagnostic design.

condition_checks.reason: Payloads sit in channels the agent reads (rendered content and UI/XML), with a payload-visibility admission rule.
No placement ablation relative to the expected target; only modality/template/repetition are varied.
Completion by adversarial state oracle plus trajectory-level hijack/awareness measures reported separately.
Nine MLLMs x two agent frameworks with per-category and per-workflow breakdowns.
RSDF localises where reasoning vs action is hijacked but there is no component/agent-graph attribution.
MRCD/RCI are fixed templates; no optimised attack with transfer/retargeting tests.
Payload presence is guaranteed by admission rules and workflows were chosen for natural third-party carriers; natural exposure rate is not estimated.
Two frameworks, nine backends, online emulator execution.
The intermediate hijack judgement relies on an LLM evaluator with unstated identity and no reported human agreement.
Black-box text templates; no white-box component.
Success conditions are registered as state oracles, but oracle code and per-instance criteria are not in the text.

Executable final-state check of adversarial goal (AGR) plus intermediate rationale/action hijack measures; shows hijacking far more frequent than completion for some models (GLM-4.6V M3A: AGR 14.81% vs RHR 77.78%).
Judge reliability not quantified (no human agreement) and labels are outcome-constrained.
Benign utility (UA) is reported with each defense.
Five standard in-context defenses are evaluated (none proposed), on one model/framework.
Generic defensive prompts give limited protection (observed finding, not a design choice).

unassigned: Reasoning-hijack onset/depth/transition-matrix diagnosis (RHOR, RHD, RATM) has no direct card; nearest is C33 (attempt vs completion) extended to step-level; candidate for a revision proposal.
revision_proposals: (single paper, not candidate) extend environmental_injection_attacks/C33 with step-level reasoning-vs-action hijack diagnosis and a warning that outcome-constrained labels make RHR/AHR partly tautological with AGR.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: report the divergence between apparent and de-confounded performance as the headline. Domain C33: report hijack attempt and attack completion separately. MobileInject's AGR (oracle completion) vs RHR/AHR/SAR (trajectory diagnosis) is that divergence.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: C02 requires ground truth independent of the evaluand; RSDF labels are LLM-produced and outcome-constrained. C33's failure mode (unvalidated judge) is present.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: instances where one axis (channel placement) varies with equal-exposure controls. Domain C30: plant natural-language instructions in attacker-writable content (messages, email, calendar, posts) of legitimate apps.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: C30 evidence is mostly web/desktop; here Android emulator workflows. Placement ablation (C30/S2) absent.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: violate the trusted-vs-untrusted boundary assumption with an exploit. Domain C34: in-context defenses (delimiters, prescriptive, SCoT, safe guide, sandwich) are the assumption being violated/tested.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: The paper evaluates defenses rather than proposing one; no adaptive attacker against a defense.

claims.text: Mobile agents are broadly vulnerable: low utility under attack and high adversarial goal success.
claims.setting: 9 MLLMs x {MobAgent, M3A}, N=108 instances each, 20-action budget, Android emulator
claims.baseline_control: UC clean utility; no human/safe-agent reference
claims.selection_vs_test: benchmark evaluation; templates authored by benchmark creators
claims.result_denominator: avg UA 17.59%/11.11%, AGR 51.13%/50.31%; per-model range AGR 24.07-83.33% (MobAgent)
claims.counterevidence: Instances are dependent (workflow x objective); UC apparently estimated from ~9 benign tasks; most conditions single-run; templated non-adaptive injections.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Under these authored templates and this emulator, all evaluated agent-model pairs show substantial AGR and low UA; not an estimate of real-world exposure.

claims.text: Cross-Modal Consistency Injection reinforces attacks beyond repeated single-channel exposure.
claims.setting: Gemini-2.5-Flash, four major benign workflows (Fig 11), 108 paired instances for reversal pattern
claims.counterevidence: One model; averaged over four workflows; dual-channel is the natural exposure for on-screen text, so the contrast partly measures realism of single-channel ablations.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On Gemini-2.5-Flash with these workflows, dual-channel placement yields higher AGR than equal-exposure single-channel controls.

claims.text: MRCD and RCI intensify trust manipulation and reasoning hijacking.
claims.baseline_control: InjecAgent+, Manipulation+, Important+ matched on length, repetition, exposure rounds, salience
claims.counterevidence: Authors' own baseline variants; single model; templates fixed.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Reinforced templates raise AGR over matched variants on one model.

claims.text: Reasoning is hijacked early and propagates to action; low AGR does not imply security.
claims.counterevidence: Labels are outcome-constrained (RHR>=AGR by construction) and produced by an unvalidated LLM evaluator; GLM-4.5V RHR=AHR identity follows from the constraint.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Tentative; the 'low AGR can hide hijacked reasoning' point is supported qualitatively by GLM-4.6V M3A (AGR 14.81 vs RHR 77.78) but coupling magnitude is not independently validated.

claims.text: Existing prompt-level defenses give limited protection.
claims.result_denominator: best SCoT 70.37% AGR (-12.96 pp, CI crosses zero), UA ~0-9%
claims.counterevidence: Only prompt-level defenses and one model/framework; no system-level isolation defenses.
claims.allowed_conclusion: For this model, five prompt defenses do not significantly reduce AGR; says nothing about other defense classes.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Executable, resettable emulator workflows with deterministic state oracles; no real-device or unseen-environment transfer.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On a 108-instance, dependent-structure emulator benchmark with authored templated injections, nine MLLMs under two agent frameworks show high oracle-verified adversarial success and low utility; on Gemini-2.5-Flash, same-content dual-channel injection beats equal-exposure single-channel controls. Reasoning-hijack coupling and the 'first benchmark' claim are not independently verified.
not_supported: Reasoning-hijack/action-hijack coupling as an independent empirical finding (partly by construction)
Generality of the cross-modal effect beyond one model/four workflows
Defense conclusions beyond prompt-level defenses on one model
unresolved: Identity and validation of the RSDF LLM evaluator
Whether apps/environment are real or mock apps
Risk-category count (9 vs 10 columns in Table 7)
assessment.retention_trace: not_applicable: benchmark/resource paper; no retained or self-improving component claimed

G.reason: Concrete, testable residue (does synchronized visual+textual exposure amplify injection; does outcome-only AGR hide hijacked reasoning) with named neighbours; neighbour comparison rests on a self-authored checklist and sources are not pinned, and dual-channel exposure is partly the natural condition.

M.reason: Design separates manipulated axis (channel), exposure confound and matched template baselines, with oracles independent of the agent and diagnostics kept separate from state verification; makes distinguishing predictions (CMCI > TOI+/VOI+, low AGR != safe). RSDF's outcome-constraining weakens independence of its diagnostics.

X.reason: Six-stage protocol, instance contract, admission rules, 20-action budget, metric definitions and equations are specified; templates, oracle code, diagnoser model/prompts, adjudication details and number of instances per category are not visible in the text.

E.measurement.reason: Deterministic state oracles for UA/AGR with replay admission are strong, but the headline diagnostic metrics (SAR/RHR/AHR, OSS) come from an unnamed LLM evaluator with no human agreement, outcome-constrained labels, ad hoc OSS weights, and UC resting on roughly nine benign tasks.

E.causality.reason: Equal-exposure and budget-matched controls plus 30/108 matched reversal trajectories give strong attribution of the cross-modal and RCI effects; limited by one model, four workflows, authored baselines, and constructed RHR/AHR coupling.

E.holdout.reason: Nine models and two frameworks give breadth, but all instances are authored templates over nine workflows (dependent), run in one emulator, no real-device check, no independent test set, defenses only prompt-level.

E.statistics.reason: N=108 per condition, cluster-paired inference for some comparisons with Holm-adjusted p-values, three-seed and repeated-run variance for a few metrics; most conditions are point estimates and a data-handling slip (swapped seed folders) is disclosed.

E.cost.reason: Equal 20-action budget for all conditions supports budget fairness; compute/time/token cost of the benchmark and of RSDF diagnosis are not reported.

rationale: MobileInject 是 evaluation_resource：108 个可复位的 Android 模拟器实例 + 确定性状态 oracle，用 CMCI（视觉/文本/双通道）配合等曝光对照、MRCD/RCI 配预算匹配基线来隔离跨模态强化效应，并用 RSDF 做轨迹诊断。强项：等曝光与 30/108 配对反转轨迹、AGR 由状态 oracle 判定。弱项：关键对照只在 Gemini-2.5-Flash 与四个工作流上；RSDF 标签来自未具名 LLM、无人工一致性，且强制与 oracle 一致使 RHR/AHR 耦合部分是构造所致；108 实例相互依赖；防御只评了 prompt 级。RS 原卡 primary=controlled_diagnostic_design/C02，supporting=assumption_audit_and_pivot；领域卡 environmental_injection_attacks/C30、C33（强）与 injection_defense_isolation/C34（部分）。claim_support=scoped，evidence_level=online。
